obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material (for example a building-systems outage across several properties, or theft of personal information)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.5)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (for example driver license numbers from visitor ID scans, employee Social Security numbers, and in some states biometric data or account credentials)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state (tenant employees, visitors, employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often the determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Vendor that maintains personal information for the company (visitor management, payroll, access control platform, property management system) has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; contracts require 24 hours (new) or 72 hours
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management and the Cyber Defense Center)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts; inherited contracts are being amended (POAM-011)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes driver license or ID numbers with a name, financial account data with access codes, and biometric data as defined in 501.702; face templates treated as biometric data pending counsel view)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if personal information was accessed. Ransomware limited to BAS servers (operational data and drawings) usually does not trigger it
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports the determination

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request; the agency may extend or revoke in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested in writing

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents personal information

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: CISA CPG 2.0 goal 5.B (voluntary); no statute requires it for this company today
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident affecting building systems
deadline: As early as practical; the runbook targets within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary and recommended (supports OFAC mitigation; may bring technical help)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours after reasonable belief that a covered incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment. Not in effect until the final rule is effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed (226.2(a)) the company would be covered because it exceeds the SBA size standard; recheck when the final rule is published

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the primary carrier's breach hotline before engaging incident vendors so costs are covered
notify: Primary carrier (then excess carriers through the broker)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Tenant notice of unauthorized access to tenant employee data (lease clauses)
citation: Lease template (2023 and later) security clause; negotiated 72-hour clauses in about 1,100 leases
trigger: Unauthorized access to tenant employee data held in the access control platform or the tenant experience platform
deadline: About 1,100 leases: within 72 hours as defined in each lease (counsel decides when each clock starts; plan from discovery). Other 2023+ leases: promptly. Older leases: no clause, but notify with the others
notify: Each tenant's designated contact, by the lease notice method (clause list in the incident binder, POAM-025)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
owner: Vice President, Leasing with the General Counsel

obligation: Tenant service interruption notices (lease clauses)
trigger: Building services degraded (HVAC, access, elevators through BAS interfaces)
deadline: Promptly; abatement clocks start after 3 business days (office, 2023 template) or 5 (retail) of untenantable premises
notify: Tenant contacts at affected properties
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SL-1 owner and JV partner notice (management agreements)
trigger: Material incident affecting managed properties, owner data, or the SL-1 services
deadline: Within 2 business days of the company's becoming aware (standard term); service interruption notices as above
notify: 6 JV partners and 9 third-party owners
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SL-2 client notice (service agreements)
trigger: Security incident affecting SL-2 client data or a platform outage
deadline: Security incident: within 72 hours of confirmation (standard term); outage: status page within 1 hour
notify: Third-party owners licensing the platform (36 buildings)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Lender notices (loan agreements)
trigger: Events the agreements define as requiring notice (for example a material adverse event or a casualty affecting collateral)
deadline: Per each agreement (Treasurer keeps the list)
notify: Lenders and agents
applies_at_this_tier: Check each agreement

obligation: Acquirer and P2PE provider notice (merchant agreement)
citation: Merchant agreement; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1 (SAQ P2PE)
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data or tampering with a P2PE terminal
deadline: Per the merchant agreement and the P2PE Instruction Manual
notify: Acquirer and P2PE solution provider
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or terminals are involved; BAS ransomware does not reach the stand-alone terminals

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or leases to federal agencies (confirmed by the General Counsel); recheck if that changes
